newsitem.title: USA: Wash. 1,158 MW nuke's output seen trimmed briefly.
newsitem.headline: Wash. 1,158 MW nuke's output seen trimmed briefly.

text.p: Washington Public Power Supply System said Thursday it expected to briefly trim the electric output at its 1,158 WNP-2 nuclear power plant to work on its recirulation pump drives.
"We need to do work on the recirculation drives," said a company spokesman.
"There's no intention to go down. It may going down to 55 to 65 percent for maybe half a day," he said, adding the generating station was operating at 90 percent of capacity.
He could elaborate at this time whether the plant would ramp down further from the current level.
He noted the company continued to adjust the new drives which were installed earlier this year. "We didn't have to shut down for those previous works," he added.
The Richland, Wash., facility is owned and operated by Washington Public Power, a consortium of 13 public utilities in the state.
All the output from WNP-2 is purchased by Bonneville Power Administration.
